senses.definition_en: An all-night thanksgiving ritual ceremony and worship cycle dedicated to Lord Shiva, performed by the Gaddi community to fulfill vows or seek divine protection.
senses.definition_hi: भगवान शिव को समर्पित रात भर चलने वाला धन्यवाद और पूजा अनुष्ठान, जो मन्नत पूरी करने या कल्याण के लिए गद्दी समुदाय द्वारा किया जाता है।
senses.definition_ur: بھگوان شیو کی نذر کی جانے والی رات بھر کی روایتی تشکر اور پوجا کی رسم، جو گدی برادری کسی منت کے پورا ہونے پر ادا کرتی ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Traditional devotional narrative ballad or sacred folk hymn recounting the legends of Lord Shiva and Parvati, sung during the night-long Nawala ceremony accompanied by the khanjari.
senses.definition_hi: भगवान शिव और पार्वती की गाथाओं का वर्णन करने वाला पारंपरिक भक्तिमय लोकगीत या आख्यान, जो नवाले के दौरान खंजरी के साथ गाया जाता है।
senses.definition_ur: روایتی مذہبی اور لوک گیت یا بیانیہ نغمہ جس میں شیو اور پاروتی کی کہانیاں بیان کی جاتی ہیں اور جو نوالہ کی رات خنجری کے ساتھ گایا جاتا ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: The iconic traditional heavy woolen homespun knee-length tunic or coat worn by Gaddi men, designed for high-altitude Himalayan pastoral life.
senses.definition_hi: गद्दी पुरुषों द्वारा पहना जाने वाला पारंपरिक घुटनों तक का भारी ऊनी चोगा या कोट, जो उच्च हिमालयी चरवाहा जीवन के अनुकूल होता है।
senses.definition_ur: گدی مردوں کا روایتی گھٹنوں تک کا بھاری اونی چوغہ یا کوٹ، جو ہمالیائی پہاڑی چرواہوں کے لیے موزوں ہوتا ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A thick, long black woolen cord or rope tightly wound around the waist over the Chola, serving as a belt, load-supporter, and storage pouch during alpine trekking.
senses.definition_hi: मोटी और लंबी काली ऊनी रस्सी जिसे कमर पर चोले के ऊपर कई बार लपेटा जाता है, जो बेल्ट, वजन संभालने और पर्वतीय यात्रा में सामान रखने के काम आती है।
senses.definition_ur: موٹی اور لمبی سیاہ اونی رسی جو کمر پر چولے کے اوپر لپیٹی جاتی ہے اور اونچے پہاڑی سفر میں وزن سنبھالنے اور بیلٹ کا کام دیتی ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Traditional wooden handloom used by Gaddi households in high-altitude hamlets for weaving woollen blankets, shawls, and garments.
senses.definition_hi: पारंपरिक लकड़ी का हथकरघा जिसका उपयोग उच्च पर्वतीय बस्तियों में गद्दी परिवारों द्वारा ऊनी कंबल, शॉल और वस्त्र बुनने के लिए किया जाता है।
senses.definition_ur: لکڑی کی روایتی ہتھ کرگھی جو اونچے پہاڑی دیہات میں گدی خاندانوں کے ذریعے اونی کمبل، شال اور کپڑے بننے کے لیے استعمال ہوتی ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A temporary seasonal migratory pastoral shelter or transit encampment used by Gaddi shepherds during their biannual transhumance journeys.
senses.definition_hi: ऋतु-प्रवास (ट्रांसह्यूमन्स) के दौरान गद्दी चरवाहों द्वारा उपयोग किया जाने वाला अस्थायी मौसमी आश्रय या पड़ाव।
senses.definition_ur: موسمی نقل مکانی کے دوران گدی چرواہوں کا عارضی قیام گاہ یا جھونپڑی۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi regional ecological / toponymic term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A thick, heavy, homespun woolen blanket or coarse cloth woven locally on traditional handlooms.
senses.definition_hi: पारंपरिक हथकरघे पर बुना गया मोटा और भारी देसी ऊनी कंबल या कपड़ा।
senses.definition_ur: مقامی ہتھ کرگھے پر بُنا ہوا موٹا اور وزنی دیسی اونی کمبل یا کپڑا۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A lighter, finely woven woolen wrap or shawl made of soft sheep wool, used for daily wear during cooler weather.
senses.definition_hi: सफेद या हल्के रंग की पतली ऊनी चादर या शॉल, जो दैनिक रूप से ओढ़ने के काम आती है।
senses.definition_ur: اون کا ہلکا اونی چادر یا شال جو روزمرہ کے استعمال کے لیے پہنی جاتی ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A heavy, thick patterned woolen blanket featuring traditional checked or striped weaves, valued for outdoor durability.
senses.definition_hi: पारंपरिक चौकोर या धारीदार बुनाई वाला भारी और मोटा ऊनी कंबल, जो अत्यंत ठंड में उपयोगी होता है।
senses.definition_ur: روایتی دھاری دار یا چوکور بناوٹ والا بھاری دیسی اونی کمبل۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A wooden drop spindle or whorl used by shepherds to spin wool by hand while walking behind their flocks.
senses.definition_hi: लकड़ी की तकली या हाथ-धुरी, जिसका उपयोग चरवाहे रेवड़ के पीछे चलते हुए हाथ से ऊन कातने के लिए करते हैं।
senses.definition_ur: لکڑی کی تکلی جس سے چرواہے چلتے پھرتے اون کاتتے ہیں۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Traditional domestic spinning wheel used by women inside households to spin sheep wool into yarn.
senses.definition_hi: पारंपरिक चरखा, जिससे घरों में महिलाएं भेड़ की ऊन से सूत और धागा कातती हैं।
senses.definition_ur: روایتی چرخہ جس پر خواتین اون کاتتی ہیں۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Traditional head cloth or veil worn by Gaddi women, pinned with decorative silver jewelry.
senses.definition_hi: गद्दी महिलाओं द्वारा सिर पर पहना जाने वाला पारंपरिक वस्त्र या दुपट्टा, जिसे चांदी के आभूषणों से सजाया जाता है।
senses.definition_ur: گدی خواتین کی روایتی اوڑھنی یا دوپٹہ۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Sheep; the central pastoral animal providing wool, milk, and subsistence in the transhumant economy.
senses.definition_hi: भेड़; गद्दी चरवाहा अर्थव्यवस्था का मुख्य पशु जिससे ऊन और आजीविका प्राप्त होती है।
senses.definition_ur: بھیڑ؛ گدی چرواہوں کا بنیادی مویشی جس سے اون اور معاش حاصل ہوتا ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Goat; companion livestock in Gaddi flocks known for leading sheep through rugged rocky terrain.
senses.definition_hi: बकरी; गद्दी रेवड़ में भेड़ के साथ पाला जाने वाला पशु जो दुर्गम चट्टानी रास्तों पर आगे चलता है।
senses.definition_ur: بکری؛ گدی ریوڑ میں پالا جانے والا جانور۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Toponym for the rugged, mountainous geographical area along the Chenab river basin in Doda and Ramban districts where northern J&K Gaddis reside.
senses.definition_hi: डोडा और रामबन जिलों में चिनाब नदी बेसिन का एक पर्वतीय क्षेत्र जहाँ गद्दी चरवाहे निवास करते हैं।
senses.definition_ur: ڈوڈہ اور رام بن اضلاع میں دریائے چناب کی وادی کا ایک پہاڑی علاقہ جہاں گدی برادری آباد ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi regional ecological / toponymic term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Flock owner or senior chief shepherd who directs seasonal grazing routes, hires assistants (pohal), and manages mountain logistics.
senses.definition_hi: रेवड़ का स्वामी या मुख्य चरवाहा जो मौसमी चराई मार्गों और सहायकों का प्रबंधन करता है।
senses.definition_ur: ریوڑ کا مالک یا بڑا چرواہا جو موسمی چرائی کا انتظام سنبھالتا ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: High mountain ridge or alpine meadow ridge pasture where sheep flocks graze during summer months.
senses.definition_hi: ऊँची पर्वत श्रेणी, कटक या अल्पाइन चरागाह जहाँ ग्रीष्मकाल में भेड़ें चरती हैं।
senses.definition_ur: اونچی پہاڑی چوٹی یا چراگاہ کا میدان جہاں گرمیوں میں بکریاں اور بھیڑیں چرائی جاتی ہیں۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi regional ecological / toponymic term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: High mountain pass traversed during biannual shepherd migrations between high alpine pastures and winter foothill valleys.
senses.definition_hi: ऊँचा पर्वतीय दर्रा जिसे चरवाहे मौसमी प्रवास के समय पार करते हैं।
senses.definition_ur: اونچا پہاڑی درہ جسے چرواہے موسمی نقل و حرکت کے دوران عبور کرتے ہیں۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi regional ecological / toponymic term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Sub-Himalayan low foothill tract, dry ravines, and scrub forests bordering the plains where Gaddis shelter flocks during winter.
senses.definition_hi: तराई और शिवालिक की निचली पहाड़ियों का क्षेत्र जहाँ गद्दी चरवाहे शीतकाल में रेवड़ चराते हैं।
senses.definition_ur: نچلی پہاڑیوں اور کھائیوں کا خشک علاقہ جہاں سردیوں میں ریوڑ رکھے جاتے ہیں۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi regional ecological / toponymic term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Sacred communal pilgrimage, mountain procession, or ritual fair held in honor of ancestral deities and Lord Shiva.
senses.definition_hi: पारंपरिक तीर्थयात्रा, धार्मिक जुलूस या देव-मेला जो कुलदेवताओं और शिव के सम्मान में आयोजित होता है।
senses.definition_ur: مذہبی زیارت، جلوس یا میلہ جو مقامی دیوتاؤں کے اعزاز میں منعقد کیا جاتا ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Traditional spirit medium or ritual oracle through whom Lord Shiva or local deities are believed to communicate during ceremonies.
senses.definition_hi: पारंपरिक आध्यात्मिक माध्यम या अनुष्ठानिक पुजारी जिसके माध्यम से देवता संचार करते हैं।
senses.definition_ur: روایتی پجاری یا وہ شخص جس پر پوجا کے دوران دیوتا کی سواری مانی جاتی ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Sacred iron trident dedicated to Lord Shiva, consecrated at high mountain passes and household shrines.
senses.definition_hi: भगवान शिव का पवित्र लौह त्रिशूल, जिसे दर्रों, पवित्र चोटियों और घरेलू वेदियों पर स्थापित किया जाता है।
senses.definition_ur: شیو کا مقدس تین نوک والا نیزہ (ترشول)۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: Sacred continuous hearth or log fire kept burning during pastoral nights and religious vigils for warmth and spiritual sanctification.
senses.definition_hi: पवित्र सतत जलती रहने वाली अग्नि या अलाव, जो चरवाहा पड़ावों और धार्मिक जागरणों में जलाई जाती है।
senses.definition_ur: مقدس آگ یا دھونی جو رات کے وقت الاؤ کی صورت میں روشن رکھی جاتی ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A small circular frame-drum or tambourine-like percussion instrument played by singers during the performance of Ainchali ballads.
senses.definition_hi: छोटा गोल डफली जैसा वाद्य यंत्र, जिसे अंचली गाते समय गायक लय देने के लिए बजाते हैं।
senses.definition_ur: ڈفلی نما چھوٹا روایتی ساز جو آنچلی گیتوں کے دوران بجایا جاتا ہے۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

senses.definition_en: A square consecrated ritual canopy constructed from timber, decorated with seasonal wild flowers and pine foliage for the Nawala ceremony.
senses.definition_hi: लकड़ी और ताजे फूलों से निर्मित चौकोर अनुष्ठानिक मंडप, जिसे नवाले की पूजा के लिए घर के आंगन में बनाया जाता है।
senses.definition_ur: پوجا کے لیے لکڑی اور پھولوں سے تیار کیا جانے والا چوکور منڈپ۔

editorial_notes: Documented as a J&K Gaddi ethnographic / material / ritual cultural term in ethnographic fieldwork. Preserved in cultural dataset; not established as an independent descriptive linguistic lexical entry.

comparative_notes: 636. Ku. poet. ṭhula dəda ‘elder brother’, ṭhula kəka ‘elder uncle’, ṭhulo baba ‘anybody older than grandfather’ with first word < OIA sthūlá- ‘large, thick, stout’ (13776) which has the following semantic parallels in the northwest and west: Ind. ghʌ̀ṽ bà̄ ‘grandfather’, Gau. ghȭ̀ ẓhⁱũ̄ ‘elder/eldest brother’ and ghȭ̀ bà̄ ‘grandfather’, Bshk. gäṇ ‘big, elder’, Sv. ghaṇyeṛo ‘elder’, Paš. gaṇ-ayōm ‘my grand-mother’, Kal. gáḍa bába ‘older sister’ and gáḍa báya ‘older brother’, Kt. gaṇvóv ‘any male relative 4 gen- erations above Ego’, K. göḍañuku bōyu ‘elder brother’, Pr. gəndar ya ‘grandfather’ — Gadd. and Pāḍ. mōṭā puttar ‘elder son’, Garh. baṛā ‘father’s elder brother’, baṛī ‘wife of father’s elder brother’, Sad. bʌḍa ‘father’s elder brother’ and bʌḍi ‘mother’s elder sister’ — G. mōṭā bhaï ‘elder brother’ (LSI ix,ii: 406), M.wār. moṭay ‘father’s mother’ and moṭeba ‘father’s elder brother’ all either < OIA ghaná-² ‘compact, firm dense’ (4424) (Ind. and Gau.) or its allomorph *ghaṇḍa- or, in case of G., Gadd. and Pāḍ. < *moṭṭa-¹ ‘defective’ (10187) or, in case of Garh. and Sad. < OIA vaṛa- ‘big’ which is, however, cognate with vr̥ddhá- ‘large; old’. There is also a semantic parallel in the very east: B.chit. ṭɔ̀̄rda ‘grandfather’ (Učida [1970: 14]) with first component < OIA sthaurá- *‘strong’ (13780) (with a doubtful modern parallel in Dardic). This is a case of intra Indo-Aryan ‘calques’ (see p. 222). Note: Semantically different is Kho. lˈoṭ bap ‘great-grandfather’ and lˈoṭ vav ‘great-grandmother’ ← lˈoṭ ‘big’ which Strand derives < OIA laṭṭa- ‘bad man’ (10917), which has in some reflexes the meaning ‘old, worn-out’.

comparative_notes: 1127. Gadd. balnā ‘to speak’ < OIA Dhātup. bhálate ‘expounds, describes’ (9406) with a modern parallel in Ash. bel- ‘to speak’. In Kal. one finds morphologically and semantically similar umbuḷík ‘to be possessed by a spirit (this is used to refer to a shaman’s action when possessed. During this time he will prophesy about the future)’ which could derive < OIA *udbhalate but much more likely is in this case Austro-Asiatic origin (see p. 980 sub ‘epilepsy’). Notes: The idea that the OIA root BHAL ‘attend to, observe’ may have developed < OIA SMR̥ ‘remember’ – for Mayrhofer BHAL . . . is probablt Middle Indo-Aryan for smārayo. . . (EWA) – is unlikely vis-à-vis the presented semantics and the fact that ‘remember’ is found in Bshk. as “shimeroo-” (Biddulph); however, note Pk. (Deś.) bhariyaṁ ‘remembered’. On the other hand, Pokorny’s suggestion that the OIA root derives < PIE *bhel- ‘schallen, reden, brüllen, bellen; resound, bark’ was apparently not accepted. Without wanting to question the difficulties found in Pokorny’s suggestion, it is worthwhile to look a little closer on modern reflexes of the two OIA verbs: (a) Modern reflexes in Outer Languages connected with the first OIA verb par- tially deviate from those found sub 9478 (bhá̄ṣate) and 9479 (bhāṣā-): Bng. bùśɛ laṇɔ ‘to talk, gossip, discuss’, Kṭg. búś and Kc. būś ‘chat, talk’, Ind. bhaṣáṽ ‘to scold’, Kal. baṣíkik ‘to boast, praise oneself’, Bhaṭ. bhaṣy ‘to talk trash’ and Ko. bās khā ‘to get a scolding; to scold; to prate’. Only West Pahāṛī Roh. bhāśṇõ ‘to promise’, quoted sub 9474, is semantically close to Medieval In- scriptional Pahāṛī, e.g. in tatsama shape Western Nepali bhāṣ (Pant [2009: 311]) and tadbhava Kumaoni paśā (M. P. Joshi [2009: 340f.]) both meaning ‘procla- mation’ or again in tatsama shape Kumaoni bhāṣa ‘bond’ (Pant loc. cit.). Neither these official-legal meanings nor several of the other here-quoted modern meanings match semantically with OIA bhāṣā- ‘speech, language (esp. common or vernacular speech, as opp. to Vedic or in later times to Sanskrit)’. However, only with Yājñavalkya and Dhūrtasamāgama the comparable meanings ‘(in law) accusation, charge, complaint, plaint’ are documented. This suggests that these meanings from the official-legal sphere are old but regionally limited. Moreover, meanings like Kal. baṣíkik ‘to boast, praise oneself’ can be due to contamination with reflexes of OIA vá̄śyate ‘roars, howls’ (11589) which is also reflected e.g. in Rom. bašaldo ‘musician’ (see p. 579). They strongly suggest ultimate Austro-Asiatic origin. Above forms beginning with m- like G. mukkō ‘kiss’, etc. have plenty of parallels in Bahnaric languages as e.g. in Laven, Cheng, Brao, Alak, Oi, Nyaheun muk all ‘kiss’. Stray cases of several of the above forms are also found in (adjacent) Tibeto-Burman languages.

Instead, since the Bng. words have parallels, a separate derivation < PIE *weng- ‘bend’ (and not < OIA BHUJ¹ ‘bend’) is suggested because the meanings differ substantially from those found sub 9522 in the following words (frequently with a > u): Gadd. bagḷū ‘a Gaddi’s purse of untanned skin (for tobacco)’ (which is also found bor- rowed into Munda Sant. bugli ‘a small bag, a purse’ and Mu. bāguli ‘a purse, pouch’), M. boṅgā ‘protuberance of a gravid womb’, Medieval Ku. buṅg ‘a hilltop where a fort is situated’ and rāj buṅg ‘royal fort’ (N. N. Misra et al. [1994: 67], but the ac- tual incomplete line of the copper plate from which the phrase is taken reads ja  vuṅgā [p. 60]); however, UGK writes sub buṅgā ‘choṭe samājoṁ ke nivās sthān (koṭ) ke buṅgā kahā jātā thā – the dwelling places of small communities (fortress, citadel, stronghold, house surrounded by a wall) used to be called buṅgā’. According to the archaeologist M. P. Joshi (pers. comm.), buṅgā is a landed estate, sometimes fortified, surrounded by hills, usually by two hills; it is not necessarily situated on a hill top, because there are Kumaoni place names like buṅgā-chīnā where chīnā means ‘ridge of a hill’, so this compound would mean ‘a fortified place on a ridge’; moreover, near village Dangoli in the Katyur Valley there is a large tract of land used for growing rice and the rice is called buṅgā kī bāsmatī; Joshi mentions also a Kumaoni word list probably from the 19th Century in which buṅgā is rendered as ‘fort-like’. The word buṅgā is mentioned for the first time in Kumaoni in the 10th Century. Edwin T. Atkinson (1973 [1882]: 507) writes about the Kumaoni King Som Chand (953-974): “When Som Chand came to Kumaon he built the first home of the Chands on the fifteen-acre plot received by him from his father-in-law and called it Ráj-búnga, which subsequently gave place to the name Champáwat.” — Kal. bạṅ ‘opening’ obviously in the sense of ‘glade, clearing’ as the following example shows: šátara bạ́ṅuna pay mo lasái, tsatrumá tay tyen ‘don’t let the goats go into that opening, the Bashgali people will beat you’ — The basic meaning of the words is perhaps best expressed in Garh. buṅgcā ‘muṛkar gol banā huā – (s.th. that got) bent into (s.th.) circular’ which makes it likely that also the following words belong to the same lemma: Bng. bukċɔ/buksɔ1 ‘blown up, inflated (e.g., cheek)’ (with -ċɔ, -sɔ suffix), and perhaps the slightly differently pronounced buksɔ2 n.m. ‘renal area’; Deog. bukċɔ n.m. ‘a filled up and baggy item (e.g. as a bag), a thick swelling (e.g. after a fall)’ (but for another interpretation see p. 981), Chin. bogśā ‘wild black conical or round mushroom’ (Kaul [2006 ii: 39]), N. buṅgo ‘cone, pod’, Jaṭ. būṅgā ‘circular stack containing straw of wheat or any other broken straw’ and P. buṅgā ‘(i) the lofty peak in which an Akālī finishes his head dress’; (ii) ‘a house, especially one of the costly buildings erected by the sardars around the Golden temple in Amritsar’ and (iii) ‘mansion’. Note: It is unclear whether Garh. buṅgṛā ‘ox, bullock of dwarf variety’ and boṅgṛo ‘a dwarf animal’ are related here.

comparative_notes: 146. Kal. brúndik ‘to grind one’s teeth together; to chew something, to grind something with one’s teeth’ as in moč kahár kái, dandọ́yak brúndin ‘when men are angry they will grind their teeth’ is probably same as Bng. mɔnṇɔ, mɔndṇɔ ‘to step on s.th., crush, tread on; to tan’ and with intensive suffix mɔndṛiaṇɔ (meanings similar to the fol- lowing Bng. words), P. mandhāṛṇā, mindhṇā ‘to crush’ and perhaps Gadd. “mandua” ‘leather pouch’ (Handa [2005: 36f.]). The words hardly derive < OIA márdati respec- tively *mṛndati ‘pounds’ (9890) which have regular reflexes with slightly different meanings in Bng. mɔṇḍakɔ n.m. ‘beat of threshing’, usually in ek mɔṇḍakɔ ‘(with) one beat of threshing’ (i.e. ‘very quickly’) (with -akɔ suffix) and mãḍṇɔ1, mãṇḍṇɔ1 ‘to tan by stamping with one’s feet; to beat’ and cf. above etymologically related Garh. māndro ‘winnowing tray, sieve’ (p. 840); Pokorny and Köbler (but not Mallory and Adams) postulate PIE *men-² ‘to step, stamp on, press together’ with e.g. Lith. minù, mìnti ‘to tan hides’. Note also Greek ματέω ‘to tread’ which Beekes derives with ques- tion mark < PIE *men- (2010: 913). EWA rejects the old idea that this root would be found in OIA carmamná- ‘tanner’ and argues for assimilation of OIA MLAI ‘wither’ (see also FLII 20.1.188); but the meaning ‘tan’ has been preserved in Bng. Here are two separate Bng. lemmata, but whether they are two different historical reflexes of the same OIA lemma or whether one is a direct PIE reflex is not completely clear. Notes: (a) Homonymous Bng. mãḍṇɔ2, mãṇḍṇɔ2 ‘to look or hunt around for’ and mã̄ḍ2 ‘need, necessity, purpose’ as e.g. in mã̄ḍ thɔi deṇi ‘what’s the point (of this)’ (besides widespread mã̄ḍ1 ‘rice broth’ which is < OIA maṇḍá- ‘scum of boiled rice’ [9735]) continues OIA (W.) maṇḍa- ‘pith, essence’. (b) Cf. also Wkh. manditk (Bellew) ‘leather’ where Morgenstierne asks (IIFL xxxv: 529) whether this is the perfect of mānd- ‘rubbed, tanned’ but the root actually means ‘rub, shampoo’. (c) Here (i.e. related with márdati) also Kal. mudhí, mundhí ‘clay’ which cf. with OIA MRAD ‘make soft’ and Wg. mŭ̄k ‘yellow clay’ < OIA *mr̥tka- ‘earth’ (10284). (d) Garh. māndro ‘(ann sambandhī bartan) dhān sukhāne ke lie – food con- nected utensil for drying paddy’ is used by Bhatt (1975 [vikrama 2032]: 395) in the sense of ‘winnowing tray’ or ‘sieve’ and thus seems to be cognate with OIA márdati ‘pounds’ (9890) (regarding semantics see there Si. ‘clean rice from the husk’). For semantically different reflexes of the OIA lemma see p. 840.

comparative_notes: 3. *drakk- ‘drag’ (6613, 14627). Has modern reflexes in Paš., Gau., Sv., Phal., Sh., Woṭ., and most probably Tor. Regarding Tōrwālī, Turner writes (14627): “Tor. (Biddulph) žigal- (prob. for ẓigal-) rather than < *jhikk-.” This is certainly correct because of Ind. ẓhikʌ́ṽ and Gau. ẓikȭ́ ‘to pull, drag’, yet, CDIAL 6613, 14627 and 5384 (*jhikk- ‘bend, jerk’) seem to be etymologically related. Here to be added are Klm. läkant LH ‘(he) is pulling’ and besides just-mentioned Ind. ẓhikʌ́ṽ “to pull; to stretch s.th.; to drag, lead an animal; to absorb’ also Kal. ẓikán ‘cowhide thongs for fastening shep- herds’ footwear’ and Bng. jìkṇɔ ‘to pull, drag; to carry (load)’. The -kk- can either be a verbal extension, *d(h)ra-kk-, or display typical word-final devoicing; in both cases the forms can go back to PIE(NW) *dʰregʰ- ‘pull, tear (out)’ which, being related with *trek- etc., seems to include irregular allomorphs. Note also Kgr. and Gadd. dharīṛnū ‘to drag’, Ḍhu-kaṛ. dhrūītē ‘having dragged’ (T. Grahame Bailey [1908: 21]), P. dhrūṇā ‘to drag’ (T. Grahame Bailey [1938: 243]) and perhaps Cam. dhrūmṇā ‘to draw’ (T. Grahame Bailey [1908: 13]). Notes: (a) Cam. dhramṇā ‘to tread upon’ is perhaps < OIA drámati ‘runs’ )loc. cit.) with spontaneous aspiration. (b) CDIAL 5384 has also been borrowed into Munda Bon. ʈiʈʈira - ǰik- ‘to pull a tendon’ (SEAlang) with second word morphologically practically same as Tor., Ind., Gau., Kal. (‘thongs’!).
